priority_meaning.P0: Blocks the relevant integration/global gate or a core promised outcome; not a CVSS/source vulnerability severity.
priority_meaning.P1: Must close before affected unit/final acceptance; does not prohibit unrelated implementation.

findings.title: The complete executable consumer catalogue is still a deliverable
findings.observed: All 82 service rows express operations as prose strings. Only 73/234 contexts carry inline historical endpoint references (185 distinct method/path pairs). The remaining 161 are not evidence of missing routes: contracts can be inherited through shared services. However, an exact current action-to-operation/schema/error/readback/consumer binding cannot be inferred from the aggregate catalogue.
findings.required_closure: Publish one versioned native capability/action bundle with stable operation IDs; protocol/handler identity appropriate to each operation; input/output/error schemas; permissions; state transitions; idempotency; recovery lookup; exact source/consumer registration and evidence. Join every feature/context/action without inventing endpoints.
findings.closure_evidence: Each required action resolves to a real registered producer and client; success, refusal, unknown and recovery have independently observed postconditions. A missing binding blocks BG-001.

findings.title: Inventory preservation does not yet provide executable per-action acceptance
findings.observed: All 349 legacy-action tests have expectation equal to the action title. There are also 34 repetitions each of generic backend positive, restart, authority and producer/consumer expectations. Detailed domain requirements may supply semantics, but these entries do not independently state the full stimulus and observable result.
findings.required_closure: Expand existing test identities with exact preconditions, input, operation/context binding, oracle, failure reason and restart/retry postcondition. Retain every legacy action and existing test identity; reusable harnesses must enumerate every bound case.
findings.closure_evidence: Traceable results cover every required action and state family; altering the postcondition or pointing a test at a sibling action causes the relevant acceptance to fail.

findings.title: 22 feature tests omit their declared primary frontend owner
findings.observed: Example: VNX-F-PRESENCE-03 declares FE-021 but its direct test belongs only to FE-017. ARTEMIS declares FE-018/test FE-017; Automation declares FE-020/test FE-019. Some of the 22 may be intentional shared delivery; this is an unclosed ownership/delegation relationship, not proof of missing implementation.
findings.required_closure: For each listed mismatch record accountable primary and supporting owners, add the primary to the applicable test binding or document and test explicit delegation. Align VNX-S-PRESENCE-05 (FE-005) with its voice feature owner and shared floating-shell responsibilities.
findings.closure_evidence: Every feature primary has a reviewed acceptance obligation in the generated plan or an explicit delegation with shared exit evidence; no feature is certified solely by an unrelated unit.

findings.title: Zero-configuration bootstrap needs an executable identity and recovery protocol
findings.observed: Signed provisioning, pairing/revocation and absence of manual host/token fields are specified. The whole-product acceptance set still needs a bound bootstrap/update/re-enrollment path with exact freshness, trust and failure semantics for the deployed Android identity and service route.
findings.required_closure: Bind first-install delivery, trust root, envelope lifetime, owner/device enrollment, endpoint/certificate rotation, device replacement/revocation, clock error, offline start and reinstall/restore to typed outcomes and actual signed-build scenarios. Preserve one owner enrollment flow without manual backend settings.
findings.closure_evidence: A fresh S24 installation reaches the intended authorized services without host/port/token entry; expired/replayed provisioning refuses; rotation and recovery work without reviving a revoked device.

findings.title: Conversation and spoken responses need a complete turn/audio contract
findings.observed: Voice is already included: streaming transcript/audio, interruption, history and speaker consent are explicit. The active entries do not supply a complete typed sequence for partial/final recognition, turn revision, command acceptance, audio playback, interruption and verified action completion, or a measurable conversation latency/quality budget.
findings.required_closure: Define session/turn/audio sequence identity, partial/final transcript and correction rules, intent ambiguity handling, TTS completion/cancellation, barge-in, text fallback, language/number pronunciation, provider failure, scoped context, redacted retention and measurable acceptance budgets. Decide supported activation modes explicitly; do not assume always-on wake word. Voice identity alone cannot replace effect authorization.
findings.closure_evidence: Positive conversations and action readback run through real speech providers; ambiguous amounts/accounts require resolution; late audio/recognition cannot restart a cancelled turn or duplicate a command; spoken done follows verified effect, not transcript receipt.

findings.title: Floating and voice lifecycle need a declared Android support matrix
findings.observed: OS permission/lifecycle preservation is required, but the release needs exact supported Android/One UI behaviour and evidence for background/locked screen, overlay, microphone, notification and audio-route restrictions. A generic persistent-assistant promise does not settle those platform cases.
findings.required_closure: Publish supported activation/foreground/background modes and fallbacks; test Bluetooth/headset changes, audio-focus loss/call, denied/revoked permission, foreground-service limits, reboot, battery saver, process death and owner dismissal on the supported S24 OS.
findings.closure_evidence: Each supported mode has actual OS readback; unsupported background behaviour is clearly surfaced with an accessible supported alternative and no silent recording.

findings.title: Strong trading specifications still need source repairs and economic proof
findings.observed: Prior pinned-source reviews/probes identify execution/TCA/slicing and model-qualification/blind-review/budget isolation work. This audit does not reassert those defects against newly deployed code. All six economic experiment templates remain NOT_RUN; a detailed learning specification is not demonstrated positive net contribution.
findings.required_closure: Reconcile each source finding at the implementation head, qualify the evaluator first, run registered full-cohort/cost/risk experiments with protected confirmation, and retain inconclusive/negative results. Demonstrate both actual outcome-to-later-decision loops and rollback.
findings.closure_evidence: Exact source tests establish repairs, and independent evidence supports each promoted policy/model at its declared scope. No profitability label follows solely from model capability or winning trades.

findings.title: Provider capability and entitlement remain external dependencies
findings.observed: The matrix contains all 82 backend units but explicitly says PREDEVELOPMENT_MATRIX_NOT_RUNTIME_PROOF. Current provider support, permitted accounts, feeds, speech access, execution/funding rails and research licences are not established by these rows.
findings.required_closure: For each required provider-operation pair bind actual account scope, entitlement, environment, source/API version, support/degradation states, rate/fee limits and qualified receipt. Select first execution/voice/data targets within existing authority; preserve all broader feature obligations or declare a separate approved scope amendment.
findings.closure_evidence: Required integrations have current permitted positive and refusal paths. Unsupported is a truthful state, not a way to count a required feature as complete; hosted fallback is tested where allowed.

findings.title: Notification and cross-surface state policy needs a complete delivery matrix
findings.observed: Canonical event identity, dedupe, quiet hours and critical-risk precedence exist. Their combinations across orb, Attention, Android notification, Floating VAN and spoken output still need explicit policy/acceptance rows, especially privacy while locked and denied OS delivery.
findings.required_closure: Specify per-channel eligibility, criticality, lock-screen masking, quiet hours, acknowledgement/snooze distinction, expiry and delivery failure. Reconcile Android permission/DND constraints with reliable in-app critical state rather than promising to bypass the OS.
findings.closure_evidence: One event remains one incident across channels; revoked/expired actions cannot execute from old notifications; critical state remains visible even when OS delivery is blocked.

findings.title: Work, agents, browser, automation and studio require operation-level lifecycle tables
findings.observed: Native identities, leases, cancellation, truthful progress, provider approvals and artifact evidence are present as rules. Per-operation conflicts, timeout/unknown reconciliation, asynchronous callbacks and partial workflow compensation must still be bound to specific native APIs and tests.
findings.required_closure: Provide transition tables for create/update/steer/pause/resume/cancel/retry and approvals, with expected revision, native operation/attempt identity, callback correlation, lease/fence, timeout and reconciliation. Explicitly define DST/misfire/overlap policy and safe file transfer retries.
findings.closure_evidence: Concurrent edits and late callbacks cannot overwrite newer state; unknown effects reconcile original operations; cancellation of a UI request never falsely reports native work cancelled.

findings.title: Privacy and erasure need a verifiable store-by-store lifecycle
findings.observed: Erasure, derivative caches, exceptions and distinction from model unlearning are explicit. The physical store/processor retention graph and deletion/restore evidence are not provided by the service catalogue.
findings.required_closure: Map source, transcript/audio, embeddings/index, cached summaries, provider retention, artifacts, telemetry and backups to policy, owner and deletion/expiry receipts. Preserve necessary audit exceptions explicitly; prevent restored backups from reviving withdrawn context.
findings.closure_evidence: A scoped erasure is traceable through each applicable store/processor and re-index/restore path; inaccessible or retained exceptions remain disclosed rather than reported as deleted.

findings.title: Recovery and capacity obligations need measurable operational budgets
findings.observed: There are candidate navigation/chart targets and qualitative recovery/capacity requirements. End-to-end availability, voice latency, event freshness, restore RPO/RTO, queue/disk limits and research-versus-protection saturation require deployed-topology budgets and failure thresholds.
findings.required_closure: Set workload-specific budgets and measurement protocols before qualification; define overload/backpressure, alert ownership, retention, restore procedure, maintenance behaviour and acceptable data loss per domain. Preserve urgent financial reconciliation independently of research load.
findings.closure_evidence: Representative load, dependency outage and restore drills meet the declared budgets or visibly degrade within policy; success is not inferred from an open port or healthy process.

findings.title: Signed app identity, upgrade and rollback need exact-build evidence
findings.observed: The blueprint preserves com.dial.van, signing/pairing continuity and compatible rollback. These requirements remain unverified for the eventual rebuilt app and current backend/store versions.
findings.required_closure: Bind signing identity, APK digest, provisioning schema, backend version compatibility, migrations, OS permissions, encrypted stores and app links to install/upgrade/rollback tests. Test rollback against newer financial data and revocations; retirement follows full parity acceptance.
findings.closure_evidence: The actual signed release installs/upgrades without orphaning owner/device state; incompatible versions refuse safely; rollback never restores obsolete authority or loses financial truth.

findings.title: Cross-domain security needs an explicit adversarial surface matrix
findings.observed: Scope, signed intents, untrusted chart/browser content, privacy and model prompt-injection boundaries are specified. Each ingress/egress and consequential command still needs exact attack fixtures and source-bound enforcement evidence.
findings.required_closure: Cover forged/replayed intents, changed confirmation arguments, cross-account/project queries, malicious shares/documents/web content, transcript ambiguity, token leakage in logs/captures, expired sessions and restored revocations. Bind denial to the actual domain owner.
findings.closure_evidence: Negative tests fail at authoritative boundaries and leave correct receipts/state; display checks or sanitized screenshots alone cannot certify authorization.

findings.title: Readability, navigation and performance remain rendered-device obligations
findings.observed: All 234 contexts inherit readability requirements, and 80 opaque colour pairs passed static arithmetic. There is no resulting proof of gradients/compositing, actual glyphs, TalkBack, large text, sunlight, battery/thermal or process-death behaviour.
findings.required_closure: Create exact-build component/state goldens and complete context/action acceptance, including both themes, 200% font scaling, focus, reduced motion, landscape/split screen, low brightness/sunlight and pending-action recovery.
findings.closure_evidence: Actual S24 receipts and accessibility/performance evidence certify the declared context/state matrix; visual degradation preserves essential controls and financial values.

findings.title: No document result currently establishes full implementation or release acceptance
findings.observed: All 1,610 application contracts are NOT_RUN. Native source admission/F15, BG and final owner/device acceptance are separate from successful document verification. Source implementation may exist elsewhere; this audit has not requalified it.
findings.required_closure: Keep an exact-source acceptance ledger across every feature/action/requirement/provider; reconcile source fixes first, qualify all backend capabilities before frontend gate, then run complete signed-app and S24 acceptance. Representative journeys discover risks but cannot certify untested siblings.
findings.closure_evidence: Current source/config/provider/build receipts support every applicable obligation and required independent/native gate. No counter, schema checker, simulator or emulator is relabelled as complete product/device evidence.
